curriculum.lesson_evidence: Water helps the body control its temperature, move nutrients around and stay alert. We lose water when we sweat, breathe and go to the toilet, so we need to drink through the day, especially when it is hot or we are active. Signs we may need a drink include thirst, a dry mouth, a headache or tiredness. Water is the best everyday drink; sugary drinks are sometimes drinks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Maya has a headache and a dry mouth after running in the sun. What could these signs mean and what should she do first?

FEEDBACK
A dry mouth and headache can be signs she needs water. She should rest in the shade, sip water slowly and tell an adult. If she feels very unwell, dizzy or confused, an adult must help straight away.

WATCH FOR
Thinking you only need a drink when you feel thirsty and that sports drinks are best. Sip water regularly, especially in heat; thirst can start after the body is already low on water.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Keep a one-day water diary: write when you drank water, how much (in cups) and how you felt. If possible compare a calm day with a very active or hot day. Write three reminders for when to drink water.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
